metadata.title: Seven Million Alerts a Night
metadata.subtitle: How AI finds exploding stars in a flood of alerts
metadata.clock: narration — per-beat durations are MEASURED, never estimated
honesty_contract: B00 is a presenter introduction and makes no factual claim.
The 7,000,000 figure is presented as the full-operations expectation, never as a present-tense measurement.
The 81-day figure is labelled DERIVED and its arithmetic is shown on screen.
Classification percentages in B11 are labelled ILLUSTRATIVE; the published figures carry their conditions.
Every astronomical image is synthetic and captioned as such.
Every beat carries a SOURCE line visible at the moment of its claim.

beats.title: Presenter introduction
beats.narration: Hi, I am Dhrumil Shah, and this video is about how artificial intelligence helps astronomers sort millions of nightly sky alerts, to find the exploding stars that are actually worth a telescope's time.
beats.scene_objective: Name the presenter, state in one sentence what the film answers, and preview the six-stage pipeline the viewer is about to travel through.
beats.visual_description: Starfield ground. 'Hi, I'm Dhrumil Shah.' in the title band; a one-line summary; then the six pipeline stages list down the vertical canvas, each with a one-phrase gloss, joined by a thin spine.
on_screen_text: How AI sorts millions of nightly sky alerts to find the exploding stars worth a telescope's time.
SCAN · SUBTRACT · ALERT · CLASSIFY · RANK · FOLLOW-UP
beats.animation_notes: Greeting rises at 0.2 s; summary at 2.6 s; the six stage rows stagger in from 5.0 s at 13-frame intervals while the spine draws down behind them; series tag at 9.6 s.
beats.sound_design: A quiet D-minor chord under the greeting; one soft rising blip per stage row.
beats.scientific_source: Presenter introduction — summarises the film; makes no factual claim

beats.title: Cold open — the flood
beats.narration: Every clear night, one telescope in Chile compares the sky to the way it looked before, and reports what changed. At full survey operations, that is about seven million alerts before morning.
beats.scene_objective: Establish the scale of the problem before any explanation.
beats.visual_description: Full-bleed drifting starfield; amber alert points ignite across the frame while a counter races to 7,000,000 under a serif title.
beats.animation_notes: Counter eased with a 0.55 power curve so the last million takes the longest; ignition threshold sweeps a seeded random field.
beats.sound_design: Alert ticks that densify with the counter.
beats.transition: Hard cut on the measured beat boundary.

beats.title: The impossible human problem
beats.narration: No group of astronomers can read seven million of anything. One alert per second, without sleeping, and a single night's take would keep you busy for eighty-one days.
beats.scene_objective: Make the volume personal: a human cannot read this.
beats.visual_description: A dark contact sheet of difference stamps scrolls behind a two-stat comparison; 1/sec resolves to 81 days.
on_screen_text: No one can read seven million.
beats.animation_notes: Slow vertical scroll of the candidate sheet; stat row rises; DERIVED flag appears after the figure, never before it.
beats.scientific_source: Derived arithmetic from S2, shown on screen

beats.title: The survey
beats.narration: The survey is the Legacy Survey of Space and Time. A very wide camera photographs the southern sky, moves on, and comes back to the same field again and again for ten years.
beats.scene_objective: Explain that the same sky is photographed repeatedly.
beats.visual_description: Bottom-up composition: sky footprints tile the upper frame and light in sweep order, a beam cone rises from an observatory silhouette below.
on_screen_text: The same sky, again and again.
LEGACY SURVEY OF SPACE AND TIME
beats.animation_notes: Sweep index interpolates across 24 tiles; freshly visited tiles flash cyan then settle.
beats.sound_design: A soft shutter per tile group.

beats.title: Reference and new
beats.narration: Every new image has an ancestor. A deep template, stacked from everything seen at those coordinates before. The pipeline aligns the two, pixel against pixel.
beats.scene_objective: Introduce the template as the thing the new image is compared against.
beats.visual_description: Two square plates stacked vertically — template above, tonight's visit below — joined by a registration rule.
beats.animation_notes: Plates rise in sequence; the registration rule draws between them.
beats.sound_design: Two soft image-load blips; a quiet alignment click.
beats.scientific_source: S1 §1 — DIA against a template of previous observations

beats.title: Difference imaging
beats.narration: Then it subtracts. Steady stars cancel. Galaxies cancel. What survives is only what changed, and anything above five sigma counts as a detection, whether it got brighter or fainter.
beats.scene_objective: Show subtraction removing everything constant, leaving only change.
beats.visual_description: New minus template resolves to a single large difference plate; a reticle closes on the residual and a ×3 zoom inset opens.
on_screen_text: POSITIVE OR NEGATIVE FLUX — BOTH COUNT
beats.animation_notes: Reticle contracts from 24% to 8.5% of the plate; zoom inset scales up from 0.86.
beats.sound_design: A descending subtraction whoosh; a detection ping on the reticle lock.
beats.scientific_source: S1 §1 — SNR > 5 in positive or negative flux

beats.title: What could it be
beats.narration: A leftover dot is not a discovery. It could be a supernova. A variable star. An asteroid. A feeding black hole. A cosmic ray striking the sensor. Or a flaw in the subtraction itself.
beats.scene_objective: Refuse the shortcut: a residual is not a supernova. Show that three causes are visually identical.
beats.visual_description: Six zoomed residual stamps in two rows of three. Row 1 (supernova, variable star, active nucleus) is indistinguishable; row 2 (asteroid, cosmic ray, artifact) is not.
on_screen_text: A dot is not a discovery.
Three different causes. One indistinguishable dot.
beats.animation_notes: Stamps rise left-to-right, row 1 then row 2; the LOOK ALIKE rule draws between the rows.

beats.title: The alert packet
beats.narration: So the pipeline packages it instead of judging it. Position, brightness, timestamp, twelve months of previous measurements, and postage stamps of the template and the difference. Requirement: out the door within sixty seconds.
beats.scene_objective: Show that the pipeline packages evidence rather than making a judgement.
beats.visual_description: A five-row packet assembles field by field beside a 60-second countdown ring; template and difference cutouts appear beneath.
on_screen_text: It packages it instead of judging.
beats.animation_notes: Rows stagger in at 16-frame intervals; ring sweeps once across the beat.
beats.sound_design: Per-row data blips; a soft ping as the countdown completes.
beats.scientific_source: S1 §1, §2.1 — packet contents; ≥98% within 60 s of readout

beats.title: The stream and the brokers
beats.narration: Now multiply that by a thousand pointings a night. The stream is public, and it is caught by seven independent community brokers built for nothing else.
beats.scene_objective: Scale the single packet up to a public stream, and name who catches it.
beats.visual_description: Packets fall continuously down seven lanes onto a rule labelled with the seven full-stream brokers; three stats below.
on_screen_text: A public stream, caught by seven.
ALeRCE AMPEL ANTARES Babamul Fink Lasair Pitt-Google
beats.animation_notes: 260 packets on independent phases and speeds; lane rules persist so the stream reads as sorted, not random.
beats.sound_design: A wash of quiet data pulses.

beats.title: Two models, one trade
beats.narration: A broker does what a tired expert would do, at machine speed. In ALeRCE, one network reads the image stamps on the very first detection. A second model waits for six, and reads the light curve instead.
beats.scene_objective: Explain what the classifier actually does, and that speed vs certainty is a design choice.
beats.visual_description: Two bordered blocks: the stamp CNN reading three cutouts into five classes; the light-curve random forest waiting for six detections.
beats.animation_notes: Block 1 rises, then block 2; the mini light curve draws and its six detection points appear in order.
beats.sound_design: Two distinct processing textures — fast for model 01, slower and lower for model 02.

beats.title: The light curve
beats.narration: Shape is what carries the meaning. A supernova climbs over days and fades over weeks. A variable star repeats itself. An asteroid simply never comes back to the same piece of sky.
beats.scene_objective: Show that shape over time is the discriminating evidence.
beats.visual_description: One large brightness-against-time plot; the supernova curve, a periodic variable, and a single asteroid point are drawn in sequence with a legend.
on_screen_text: ILLUSTRATIVE CURVE SHAPES — NOT FITTED TO ANY OBSERVED EVENT
beats.animation_notes: Each trace draws by stroke-dashoffset in narration order: supernova, variable, then the asteroid point.
beats.sound_design: A single low blip on the asteroid point.
beats.scientific_source: S5 — hierarchical taxonomy: transient / periodic / stochastic

beats.title: Probabilities, not a verdict
beats.narration: And the answer is not a verdict. It is a set of probabilities. The stamp classifier is about ninety percent accurate on a balanced test set, which is a statement about the model, not about the star.
beats.scene_objective: Represent uncertainty correctly and separate illustrative output from published performance.
beats.visual_description: Four probability bars grow to illustrative values; beneath them a bordered panel carries the two real published numbers with their conditions.
beats.animation_notes: Bars and their numerals grow together so a value is never shown before its bar earns it.
beats.scientific_source: S5 — 90% balanced-test-set accuracy; 81% recall on TNS-confirmed SNe

beats.title: Prioritisation
beats.narration: But that is enough to sort. Thousands of ordinary alerts sink quietly. A few unusual ones rise to the top of somebody's queue before the night is over.
beats.scene_objective: Name the model's actual contribution: ordering, not truth.
beats.visual_description: A queue of synthetic alert IDs; the tracked candidate lifts from ninth to first while the rest sink and fade.
on_screen_text: ILLUSTRATIVE QUEUE — IDS AND SCORES ARE SYNTHETIC
beats.animation_notes: Hero row interpolates upward while lower rows fade by vertical position — the vertical canvas does the work.
beats.sound_design: A soft whoosh as rows slide; a confirming ping as the candidate reaches first place.
beats.scientific_source: S4 — brokers filter, cross-match, classify and prioritise for follow-up

beats.title: Follow-up and spectroscopy
beats.narration: And sorting is the whole point, because the confirming measurement is rare. A spectrum splits the light into wavelengths and shows what is actually burning. Very few telescopes can spare the time.
beats.scene_objective: Introduce the measurement that actually determines identity.
beats.visual_description: An observatory dome slews, then a spectrum draws: a continuum with broad absorption troughs, labelled blue to red.
on_screen_text: A SECOND FACILITY SLEWS TO THE COORDINATES
SPECTRUM — THE LIGHT, SPLIT BY WAVELENGTH
beats.animation_notes: Dome rotates 26° to −12° on a fixed pier; the spectrum draws left to right after the slew settles.
beats.sound_design: Dome rotation rumble; a sustained chord as the spectrum resolves.
beats.scientific_source: S9 — prioritising events for spectroscopic follow-up

beats.title: The limit
beats.narration: Rubin may find close to a million supernovae. The overwhelming majority will never get a spectrum at all. A classification is a ranking. It is not a confirmation.
beats.scene_objective: State plainly that classification is not confirmation, and quantify the gap.
beats.visual_description: A 40×25 dot field where each dot is ~1,000 supernovae; 3% light green. Two stats and a pull-quote beneath.
on_screen_text: A ranking is not a confirmation.
EACH DOT ≈ 1,000 SUPERNOVAE RUBIN MAY FIND
It decides where the scarce measurement gets spent.
beats.animation_notes: Dots reveal in index order so the lit fraction is seen to be small rather than asserted to be.
beats.sound_design: Score only — no effects under the thesis line.
beats.scientific_source: S7 / S8 — ~1M SNe expected; ~30,000 planned spectra (TiDES)

beats.title: Close
beats.narration: The machine never decides what exploded. It decides what is worth pointing a telescope at, while there is still something left to see.
beats.scene_objective: Land the thesis in one line and return to the opening image.
beats.visual_description: Back to the starfield with a single pulsing amber point; title restate, closing line, presenter card.
on_screen_text: The machine decides what is worth pointing a telescope at.
beats.animation_notes: Point pulses on a slow sine; title and closing line rise; an amber rule anchors the presenter card.
beats.transition: Held tail after the last word.
beats.scientific_source: Presenter conclusion — restates the cited limit, asserts no new result
